papers.title: THE ROLE OF VITAMIN D DEFICIENCY IN THE DISRUPTION OF OSSEOINTEGRATION PROCESSES OF DENTAL IMPLANTS
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes scientific evidence on the potential role of vitamin D deficiency in impaired osseointegration of dental implants. The aim is to examine the relationship between vitamin D status, peri-implant bone formation, and clinical implant outcomes. The biological rationale for the effects of vitamin D on bone metabolism, the assessment of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations, and considerations in interpreting this marker are discussed. Particular attention is paid to distinguishing experimental findings, clinical associations, and evidence supporting the effectiveness of correcting vitamin D deficiency. Research limitations related to differences in laboratory criteria, follow-up periods, and coexisting risk factors are considered. The need for further controlled clinical studies is emphasized to clarify the prognostic significance of vitamin D deficiency and evaluate whether its correction improves dental implant outcomes.

papers.title: Early Stability Dynamics of UV-Functionalized Dental Implants Under Early Loading: Evaluating ISQ Changes in the Posterior Mandible
papers.abstract: Background UV photofunctionalization has been proposed as a method to enhance implant surface bioactivity and potentially improve early osseointegration. Objective This study aimed to evaluate early implant stability under early loading conditions by analyzing changes in Implant Stability Quotient (ISQ) values over time. Methods This case series included three implants placed in the posterior mandible and treated with UV photofunctionalization for 24 hours prior to placement. Implant stability was assessed using Resonance Frequency Analysis (RFA) at baseline (implant placement), at 3 weeks, and at 4 weeks prior to functional loading. Insertion torque values were recorded at the time of implant placement. Results A progressive increase in ISQ values was observed across all cases, ranging from 77 to 85, with no evidence of a stability dip during the study period. Conclusions Within the limitations of this case series, the observed ISQ progression indicates a favorable stability pattern under early loading conditions. However, due to the small sample size and absence of a control group, no definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding the specific effect of UV photofunctionalization.

papers.title: Buckling behavior and interpretable machine-learning of CFRP-strengthened circular steel tubes under axial compression
papers.abstract: This study develops a physics-informed and interpretable data-driven framework for predicting the axial buckling capacity of circular steel tubes strengthened with longitudinal CFRP strips. A validated finite element (FE) model against test results was used to generate 196 parametric samples, and these data were combined with 190 experimental results from literature to establish a 386-sample database for machine-learning modeling. The FE analysis shows that CFRP strengthening increases the sectional flexural stiffness and can improve the ultimate load by up to 49.57% for slender members. For medium-length columns, a distinct capacity jump of up to 30.12% is observed, which is attributed to a transition from global flexural buckling to localized instability induced by the longitudinal stiffness constraint of high-modulus CFRP strips. Four prediction models (XGBoost, BPNN, SVR and Stacking) were optimized using four swarm-intelligence algorithms to overcome the sensitivity of model performance to hyperparameter selection. Pearson correlation analysis identifies the slenderness ratio as the dominant capacity-reducing variable ( r = -0.81), whereas the number of CFRP layers, the diameter-to-thickness ratio and the steel yield strength show positive correlations with buckling resistance ( r = 0.25, 0.25 and 0.13, respectively). Among all optimized models, AVOA-XGBoost provides the best overall performance, with a testing R 2 of 0.925, a MAE of 18.40 kN and a RMSE of 30.11 kN. SHAP analysis further confirms that the learned feature effects are consistent with structural stability theory. The proposed framework offers both mechanistic insight into CFRP-assisted instability control and a practical surrogate model for the rehabilitation design of steel tubular members.

papers.title: THE INFLUENCE OF VITAMIN D, MAGNESIUM, AND ZINC LEVELS ON THE OSSEOINTEGRATION OF DENTAL IMPLANTS: CLINICAL AND BIOCHEMICAL ASPECTS
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the clinical and biochemical aspects of the potential influence of vitamin D, magnesium, and zinc status on the osseointegration of dental implants. The aim is to summarize scientific evidence on the relationship between the status of these micronutrients and the formation and remodeling of peri-implant bone tissue. The mechanisms through which they participate in mineral metabolism, regulate bone cell activity, and contribute to reparative processes are examined. Particular attention is given to comparing biochemical indicators with clinical parameters, including implant stability, changes in marginal bone levels, and the incidence of early complications. The article discusses the potential role of assessing serum concentrations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D, magnesium, and zinc when planning implant treatment, as well as the limitations involved in interpreting these indicators. The importance of distinguishing experimental findings from clinical observations is emphasized. Current evidence does not establish conclusively that each of the micronutrients considered independently influences the success of dental implant treatment. A promising direction for future research is the conduct of prospective studies that account for comorbidities, dietary patterns, bone tissue status, and implant placement protocols.

papers.title: Advances in Reconstructive Plastic Surgery: From Skin Grafts and Microsurgery to Tissue Engineering, Artificial Intelligence and 3D Bioprinting — A Narrative Review of Evolution, Clinical Applications, Emerging Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Reconstructive plastic surgery has evolved from relatively simple techniques of wound closure and skin replacement into a multidisciplinary field capable of restoring increasingly complex anatomy and function. Skin grafts and local or regional flaps remain indispensable because they are reliable, accessible and clinically established, while microsurgery has expanded the ability to transfer vascularized tissue to defects created by trauma, burns, cancer, congenital anomalies and other conditions. At the same time, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have introduced a different objective: rather than merely replacing missing tissue, the field increasingly seeks to recreate biological environments that support regeneration, vascularization, innervation and long-term functional integration. This narrative review examines that transition and integrates conventional reconstructive surgery with contemporary advances in biomaterials, stem-cell-based therapies, tissue-engineered skin, vascular and nerve engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, digital surgical planning, artificial intelligence (AI), robotic microsurgery and emerging digital-twin concepts. Particular attention is given to the persistent translational barriers that separate promising laboratory demonstrations from routine clinical treatment, including vascularization, cell survival during printing, innervation, immune response, mechanical integration, long-term durability, manufacturing, cost and regulatory uncertainty. AI is examined as an enabling technology rather than a replacement for surgical judgment, with applications in virtual surgical planning, image analysis, flap-risk prediction and postoperative monitoring. Evidence summarized in the supporting research material indicates that virtual planning can improve geometric accuracy and that machine-learning systems may assist in risk stratification and monitoring, but external validation and prospective clinical evaluation remain essential. The review concludes that the most credible future is not the disappearance of conventional reconstruction but the convergence of microsurgery, regenerative biology, advanced biomaterials, computational planning, AI and biofabrication. The central trajectory of the field is therefore a shift from replacement toward regeneration, with the long-term goal of producing patient-specific tissues that are vascularized, innervated, mechanically appropriate and functionally integrated.

papers.title: Transfer learning on frequency-domain data of vehicle finite-element-simulations in vibroacoustics
papers.abstract: In the early stages of vehicle development, surrogate models and machine learning play an increasingly important role. In order to optimize the sound in the interior efficiently, engineers use surrogate models of finite element simulations to minimize high-priced hardware tests. Surrogate models based on neural networks have a high demand of time-consuming simulations to provide a sufficient data basis for training, validation, and testing. In this work, simulations from real development processes are used to investigate the methodology of transfer learning to lower this demand. The transfer learning methodology uses a pre-trained neural network of vehicle A to train a surrogate model for vehicle B with significantly less data. The data basis consists of mechanical point admittances from vibroacoustic simulations in the frequency-domain, which characterize the vibration propensity of a structure and describe a typical evaluation parameter in vibroacoustics. We evaluate this methodology of transfer learning for different vehicles based on the performance of the neural networks. With good performance of the transfer learning step, time-consuming finite element simulations can be saved to train surrogate models for vehicle design. To the best of our knowledge, the investigation of transfer learning on time-consuming, real-world production finite element simulations of different vehicles has not been available in the literature yet. Furthermore, this work is characterized by frequency-domain data.

papers.title: Riemannian Geometry of Latent Spaces: From Vector Fields to Curvature in Geometric World Models: A Synthesis of Differential-Geometric Foundations for Geometry-Aware Latent Dynamics
papers.abstract: This article synthesises the differential-geometric foundations underlying geometric world models, beginning from the role of vector fields on latent Riemannian manifolds and proceeding through the Riemannian metric and its inverse, the transformation properties of vectors and covectors, the Levi-Civita connection, and the Riemann curvature tensor. Drawing on recent expositions of vector fields for geometric world models, we develop a coherent account of why the latent space of a world model is properly treated as a Riemannian manifold, how the Riemannian gradient is obtained by raising the index of the differential with the inverse metric, and how the Levi-Civita connection and Riemann tensor furnish the intrinsic calculus of parallel transport, geodesics, and curvature required for geometry-aware planning and optimisation. The treatment is self-contained and emphasises the coordinate-independent character of the constructions.

papers.title: A Bayesian-guided aggregation-disaggregation algorithm for transit planning
papers.abstract: Public transit is essential for daily mobility, especially for individuals without access to private vehicles. At the same time, designing efficient transit systems remains challenging when demand is spatially dispersed, density is low, and operational resources are constrained. This paper introduces an integer programming model for transit system planning based on a many-to-many (M2M) matching framework. The framework captures detailed routing decisions of the transit fleet while accounting for vehicle capacity, transfer constraints, and user-perceived service quality. To address the scalability challenges of solving this model, we propose a hybrid solution approach that integrates Bayesian optimization (BO) with a structured aggregation-disaggregation (A-D) procedure. In this solution framework, aggregation abstracts the original network into a reduced representation, enabling efficient solution of a smaller and more tractable problem. Disaggregation then maps the resulting aggregated solution back to the original network. Bayesian optimization guides the search over the space of possible network aggregations, enabling efficient evaluation of candidate aggregations that yield high-quality disaggregated transit plans. We evaluate this approach in a real-world case study using data from Benton Harbor, Michigan, U.S.A. Experimental results show that our framework reliably identifies high-quality solutions in settings where the direct M2M solver is unable to produce feasible solutions or delivers consistently weak performance. In addition, the Bayesian-guided exploration markedly improves the efficiency of searching over candidate aggregations compared to random search, enabling efficient discovery of promising network aggregations.

papers.title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
papers.abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.

papers.title: Data-Driven Flipping Engineering for High Thermal Anisotropy in Janus Two-Dimensional Materials
papers.abstract: Abstract The vertical integration of heterogeneous dies in three-dimensional integrated circuits demands materials with extreme thermal anisotropy to dissipate heat in-plane while suppressing cross-plane leakage. Randomly twisted van der Waals stacks can enhance anisotropy, but their stochastic nature lacks precise control. Here, we report flipping engineering in Janus MoSSe stacks, exploiting the intrinsic asymmetry between the S–Mo–Se and Se–Mo–S terminations as a programmable structural degree of freedom orthogonal to twisting. By integrating machine-learned potential molecular dynamics with Bayesian optimization for a 14-layer MoSSe stack, we identify a structure with strongly suppressed effective cross-plane thermal conductivity of 0.082 ± 0.002 W m–1 K–1 at 300 K while maintaining robust in-plane conduction, yielding an anisotropy ratio of about 760 and 35% higher than the crystalline reference. This effect arises from flipping-induced breaking of stacking periodicity, which perturbs midfrequency phonons (2–8 THz) and leads to band splitting and nearly flat, layer-localized modes. These changes reduce the cross-plane propagating channels and thus weaken their contribution to thermal transport, while their impact on in-plane transport dominated by low-frequency acoustic phonons is negligible. Flipping engineering thus provides programmable stacking-sequence strategy and a versatile route for designing anisotropic properties in layered materials.

papers.title: Experimental investigation and multi-objective optimization of key control parameters for low-emission heavy-duty hydrogen engines
papers.abstract: With the increasing global energy demand and the advancement of carbon neutrality goals, efficient and low-carbon power systems have attracted extensive attention in heavy-duty engine research. Hydrogen, as a clean and sustainable fuel, shows considerable potential for heavy-duty engine applications. However, optimizing key control parameters to simultaneously improve performance and reduce emissions remains a major challenge. This study combines experimental investigation with multi-objective optimization to provide a systematic assessment of the influence of key control parameters, including the excess air coefficient (λ), spark timing(ST), and throttle position opening(TPO), on the combustion, performance, and emissions of heavy-duty hydrogen engines. The results indicate that increasing λ effectively reduces nitrogen oxide (NO x ) emissions, ST significantly affects combustion characteristics, and TPO strongly influences power output. Reasonable regulation of these critical control parameters plays a vital role in enhancing the overall performance of hydrogen engines. By employing the Bayesian Optimization-Extra Trees (BO-ET) algorithm and the multi-objective whale optimization algorithm (MOWOA), this study performs multi-objective optimization of a hydrogen engine with respect to power, brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC), and NO x emissions. The optimization outcomes show that the hydrogen engine attains a power output of 96.06 kW, a BSFC of 75.31 g/kWh, and NO x emissions of 19.77 ppm. Relative to the reference operating condition from previous experiments (TPO of 40%, ST of −24.8 °CA ATDC, λ of 2.5, and peak in-cylinder pressure of 74.66 bar), the optimized condition maintained comparable power and BSFC while significantly reducing NO x emissions by 76.5%, demonstrating a pronounced optimization effect.

papers.abstract: Fiber lasers are widely used in advanced manufacturing and aerospace due to their high beam quality, compactness, and operational stability. However, as laser power density and integration level continue to increase, thermal management becomes a key factor limiting performance and service life. This study proposes a data-efficient design framework for a refrigerant-based cold plate applied to fiber-laser cooling. A multi-objective optimization strategy is developed by combining a multi-fidelity surrogate with Bayesian optimization, where pressure drop and mean absolute temperature deviation are treated as conflicting objectives. In addition, Shapley additive explanations analysis is introduced to interpret the influence of structural parameters on thermo-hydraulic performance. The results show that the multi-fidelity surrogate model improves predictive accuracy by 29%–43% compared with single-fidelity surrogate model while significantly reducing the number of expensive high-fidelity simulations. The optimized design achieves a substantial reduction in flow resistance with only a limited thermal-performance penalty. Experimental results further show that, under a heat load of 2800 W, the optimized cold plate reduces flow resistance by 42.5%, while the average surface temperature in the critical region increases by only 1.7 °C relative to the reference design. The proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable solution for the structural design of compact, high-performance refrigerant-cooled cold plates for high-power laser devices.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Lightweight and Heavyweight Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Apple Leaf Disease Classification
papers.abstract: Leaf diseases can significantly reduce both the productivity and quality of crops; therefore, early and accurate diagnosis is required for sustainable farming. Reliance on visual examination by experts is time-consuming and expensive and may result in inconsistent or inaccurate diagnoses. The present study investigated a deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for the automatic classification of apple leaves into three classes, namely, Alternaria blotch, Marssonina blotch and healthy leaves. A field dataset of 9,000 images was acquired with a mobile phone in orchards of Himachal Pradesh under natural lighting, from different shooting angles, and with natural backgrounds. Ten pre-trained CNN models, five lightweight and five heavyweights were evaluated and compared using transfer learning, and each model was trained three times with different random seeds to check the statistical reliability of the results. EfficientNetV2B0 and DenseNet201 were identified as the best lightweight and heavyweight models, achieving mean accuracies of 94.30% and 92.96%, respectively. Both models were subsequently fine-tuned using hyperparameters selected through Bayesian optimization, which raised their accuracies to 98.07% and 96.00%, respectively. The fine-tuned EfficientNetV2B0 performed significantly better than the fine-tuned DenseNet201 while using about one-third of the parameters, and running nearly five times faster on a CPU. A well-optimized lightweight network can, therefore, outperform a much larger one and remain practical for mobile and Internet of Things (IoT) use. This study offers a practical and efficient approach with strong potential for adaptation to other crops, and integration into mobile and IoT-based disease diagnosis systems.

papers.title: Stochastic SEIR dynamics via graph Laplacian diffusion under transmission uncertainty
papers.abstract: Epidemic spatial spread across interconnected populations depends on both mobility between locations and random fluctuations in transmission. We extend the Susceptible-Exposed-Infected-Removed (SEIR) epidemic model to a network setting by introducing graph Laplacian diffusion to capture population mobility, and further incorporate stochastic perturbations in the transmission rate to capture environmental noise. Using Lyapunov function analysis, we first establish that the stochastic system admits a unique global solution which remains non-negative for all time, so that the model is mathematically well-posed and its state variables retain their epidemiological meaning as population counts. Building on this well-posedness, we then apply Lyapunov techniques a second time to analyse the long-term behaviour of the solution. The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be globally asymptotically stable when the basic reproduction number does not exceed one, indicating disease extinction. When the basic reproduction number exceeds one, the disease instead persists, in the sense that the stochastic solution exhibits a bounded time-averaged deviation from the endemic equilibrium of the corresponding deterministic system. Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods are further employed for parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification, applied to COVID-19 incidence data across all 47 prefectures in Japan. The proposed framework brings together network-driven mobility, stochastic transmission dynamics, and Bayesian uncertainty quantification within a SEIR model. Finally, computational experiments on a small-world Watts-Strogatz network are used to validate and visually illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Using Photovoice to Examine Student Learning in Graduate Health Administration: A Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) Study
papers.abstract: This pilot study explores the use of photovoice as an experiential learning (EL) tool in graduate health administration education, focusing on concepts related to the Social Determinants of Health (SDOH). The project engaged 51 graduate students across 3 in-person health administration courses in a 6-week assignment involving original photography and a descriptive narrative (up to 250 words) to reflect on observed SDOH in their communities. Data were collected via the graded student assignments and a subsequent open-ended reflection survey. Employing a Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) approach, the systematic analysis of the qualitative data revealed four major themes: (1). Recognizing Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) and Societal Impact; (2). Connecting Personal Experience to Professional Identity; (3). Building Systems Thinking and Applied Insight; and (4). Reimagining Learning through Experiential Reflection. These findings demonstrate how integrating participatory and experiential pedagogies cultivates purposeful reflection, applied problem-solving, and professional competencies crucial for future health promotion leaders. The study fulfills the goal of SoTL scholarship by disseminating findings to refine course design and enhance student understanding of complex health inequities.

papers.title: Physics-guided data-driven learning with active learning for slope stability analysis considering spatial variability
papers.abstract: The spatial variability of soil properties significantly affects slope stability and failure mechanisms, introducing uncertainties in the factor of safety ( F s ), deformation responses, and critical slip surfaces (CSS). Traditional Monte Carlo-based random field methods are computationally expensive, while passive sampling-based machine learning models often suffer from inefficient data utilization. This study develops a physics-guided data-driven learning framework with active learning (PGDAL) for spatially variable slope stability analysis. The framework integrates MNMM-based high-fidelity simulations, active learning-based sample selection, and CNN/U-Net surrogate models. Spatially varying soil properties are represented as image-based inputs, while F s , displacement fields, strain fields, and CSS information obtained from MNMM simulations are used as learning targets. Four query strategies, including LCUS, margin sampling, entropy sampling, and maximum standard deviation sampling, are compared to evaluate their effects on model performance. The proposed framework enables multi-response prediction by learning the nonlinear relationship between random field inputs and slope responses, and further identifies smooth CSS through predicted deformation fields. Results demonstrate that PGDAL achieves higher prediction accuracy and faster convergence than passive sampling while requiring fewer high-fidelity samples. The proposed framework provides an efficient surrogate modeling approach for intelligent slope stability analysis considering spatial variability.

papers.title: Current Management and Outcomes of Femoral Neck Fractures in Older Adults in Yaoundé, Cameroon: A Six-year Study of 74 Cases
papers.abstract: Background: Femoral neck fractures are common among older adults and are associated with high morbidity and mortality. The main challenges are reducing mortality and improving functional outcomes. Aim: This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, management, and outcomes of femoral neck fractures in Yaoundé. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study over 6 years and 5 months, from 1 January 2018 to 31 May 2024. The target population comprised patients with femoral neck fractures followed at six major hospitals in the capital city of Yaoundé. Results: Of 5,950 patients hospitalised in orthopaedic units across the six hospitals, 129 patients (prevalence 2.18%) had 130 femoral neck fractures, including one bilateral fracture. We included 74 patients, with a mean age of 64.34 ± 18.2 years. Men predominated, with a sex ratio of 1.24. Low-energy falls in older adults were the mechanism in 75.5% of cases. Comorbidities included hypertension (25.7%), HIV (12.1%), and diabetes mellitus (9.5%). Forty-two fractures occurred on the right and 32 on the left. Garden types I, II, III, and IV accounted for 1.35%, 8.11%, 43.24%, and 47.30% of fractures, respectively. The median delay from fracture to hospital arrival was 1 day, and the median delay to surgery was 16.5 days. Management comprised total hip arthroplasty (6.67%), hemiarthroplasty (48%), open reduction and internal fixation osteosynthesis (20%), and non-operative management (25%). The median postoperative stay from surgery to discharge was 11 days. Major complications included anaemia (65.2%), dislocation (15.6%), surgical site infection (11.7%), and fixation failure (3.8%). Blood transfusion was administered to 54 patients (72.97% of the 74-patient cohort). Nine patients (17.6%) underwent reoperation. The 1-year mortality rate was 17.6%. Good-to-excellent hip scores were recorded in 51% of patients. The median follow-up was 280 days (range, 1 month to 5 years and 8 months). Conclusion: Femoral neck fractures were associated with substantial delays to surgery. Approximately one-fifth of patients died within the first year, and functional outcomes require improvement.

papers.abstract: Background: pH-responsive hydrogels are promising materials for controlled drug delivery because changes in environmental pH can influence polymer ionization, network swelling, and molecular transport. However, predicting drug-release behaviour and interpreting associated measurements remain challenging because of the coupled effects of polymer chemistry, drug diffusion, and measurement uncertainty. Mathematical modelling, quantum-dot-based optical transduction, and electronic signal processing provide complementary approaches for investigating these processes. Objective: This study proposes an integrated computational framework combining pH-responsive hydrogel drugrelease modelling, quantum-dot-assisted optical sensing, electronic signal processing, and mathematical optimization. Methods: The framework is centred on a poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate-co-methacrylic acid) (pHEMA-coMA) hydrogel containing phenylpropanolamine as a reference drug. The proposed model connects pH-dependent hydrogel swelling with drug transport and release. A virtual quantum-dot optical module is introduced to represent a calibrated concentration-dependent measurement response, while an electronic signal-processing module is designed to examine the effects of sampling, measurement noise, baseline variation, and digital filtering. papers.title: Optimal configuration of complementary coupled energy supply stations for remote offshore hydrogen refueling and charging
papers.abstract: With the implementation of China's “offshore hydrogen island” project and the development of hydrogen and electric ships, the proposal of “renewable energy + energy storage + combined hydrogen production” has opened up new ideas for remote offshore energy supply. However, extending the cruising range of deep-ocean unmanned ships without requiring them to pull into shore remains a critical logistical and economic challenge. To address this gap and move beyond conventional single-energy platforms, a novel wind turbine-driven complementary coupled energy supply station for remote offshore hydrogen refueling and charging is proposed. This system aims to meet the daily electricity demand of 50 electric ships and the hydrogen refueling demand of 1000 kg, introducing a dual-timescale hybrid storage architecture. The energy station incorporates elements of wind energy, electrolyzers, fuel cells, hydrogen storage, and electricity storage. Based on 24-h hourly wind speed and load profiles from four typical seasonal days, which serve as representative operational boundaries and peak stress scenarios to guide year-round capacity optimization, a nested two-layer optimization framework combining Bayesian Optimization with Particle Swarm Optimization is used to obtain the optimal capacity configuration. The system is evaluated based on three proposed indexes: the system cost of power, the system cost of hydrogen, and the system cost of energy. Comparative analysis shows that the energy supply station with a fuel cell performs significantly better. It achieves a system cost of power of 0.1789 $/kWh and a system cost of hydrogen of 4.9873 $/kg, which are 29.62% and 35.28% lower, respectively, than the configuration without a fuel cell. This validates the advantage of the hybrid energy storage system, where batteries manage short-term intra-day fluctuations, and hydrogen storage successfully addresses multi-day to cross-seasonal energy deficits. Sensitivity analysis reveals that the lithium-ion battery is the most influential component regarding overall system costs. Finally, the conditions for flexible operation under varying load shares are derived. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that the proposed multi-energy station is highly cost-efficient, providing a robust, scalable engineering blueprint for the design of future remote offshore green energy infrastructure.

Taking the stable tracking of output voltage as the core objective, the model predictive control (MPC) model of the converter is constructed based on state-space equations, and an error correction method is introduced as the feedback correction link to eliminate the steady-state error caused by parameter mismatch. Second, the power regions are divided by combining the zero-voltage switching (ZVS) turn-on conditions and the backflow power optimization criteria. Finally, the experimental verification results show that the proposed control strategy can achieve ZVS turn-on of power switches, effectively reduce backflow power and improve the dynamic performance of the system.

papers.title: Uncertainty analysis of hydrogen spark-ignition engine parameters
papers.abstract: Predictive engine simulations require rigorous assessment of how uncertainties in operating conditions and model parameters propagate through thermodynamic and combustion models. Despite the growing interest in uncertainty quantification (UQ) in engine research, existing efforts remain largely limited to measurement uncertainty or isolated sub-models, while comprehensive UQ applied to predictive system-level engine models is still lacking. This need is particularly acute for hydrogen/air spark-ignition combustion in spark-ignition engines (SIE), where strong thermo-diffusive effects and a high sensitivity to operating conditions challenge simulation robustness. This work proposes a complete UQ framework applied to a predictive 0D combustion model for SIE. A 0D version of the Coherent Flame Model (CFM), adapted to incorporate Markstein effects, is calibrated for propane and hydrogen. A surrogate-based UQ methodology is developed, combining global sensitivity analysis and uncertainty propagation to efficiently explore the influence of parameter uncertainty. This methodology is then applied to several uncertainty scenarios. First, a configuration representative of limited available data, characterized by large uncertainty ranges, is considered. Second, a configuration reflecting well-instrumented experimental conditions, with tighter uncertainty bounds, is analyzed. The results are strongly dependent on the selected scenario. In the data-limited case, the analysis identifies intake pressure, equivalence ratio, and compression ratio as the dominant contributors to output uncertainty, with hydrogen exhibiting increased sensitivity to mixture preparation and moderately higher overall uncertainty levels. In the second scenario, uncertainty levels are significantly reduced, and the dominant contributors are intake pressure and cylinder wall temperatures. Furthermore, the trapped mass is shown to depend jointly on intake pressure and wall temperature, demonstrating that Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) boundary-condition calibration cannot rely solely on intake-pressure adjustment. Overall, the study establishes a general methodology for uncertainty analysis of predictive 0D combustion models and provides actionable guidance for the specification of boundary conditions in CFD simulations.

papers.abstract: Abstract Direct CO2 hydrogenation to aromatics (CTA) offers a sustainable alternative to petroleum-based aromatic production, yet its catalyst design is severely hindered by data scarcity, feature heterogeneity, and conflicting multiobjective requirements. Therefore, this study proposes a generative enhancement and manifold preservation-driven interpretable machine learning (GEMP-ML) framework. It integrates heuristic hybrid encoding, hierarchical missing value management, generative data augmentation, and active-learning-based sample screening to construct an information-enriched catalyst training set. To enable semantically faithful numerical representation of high-cardinality categorical features, a best-first sampling strategy is designed to identify the optimal hybrid encoding scheme from 89 candidate combinations specifically for these categorical variables. Combined with hierarchical semantic missing-value management and high-fidelity imputation algorithms, the data integrity of the CTA dataset is restored while preserving the semantic integrity of categorical features. GMM-based generative augmentation combined with diversity-aware active learning improved the utilization of synthetic data, and the CatBoost surrogate model achieved an average test set R2 of 0.973 across the three targets. Complementary interpretability analysis further identifies key descriptors governing catalyst performance, guiding the Pareto optimization of catalyst formulations and operating parameters. The recommended Zn–Al/HZSM-5 catalyst is predicted to achieve approximately 36.5% CO2 conversion, 78.6% C5+ selectivity, and 0.35% CO selectivity. The model is further validated against two independent experimental datasets covering 100 h time-on-stream, with prediction errors of <8%, supporting its ability to reproduce the observed performance trends under the evaluated conditions. This generalizable framework provides a systematic, data-driven paradigm for accelerating the design of high-performance catalysts in data-sparse catalytic systems.

Traditional image‑based classification methods are limited by factors such as illumination, occlusion, and surface treatment, making it difficult to effectively distinguish different materials using visual features alone. To address this problem, an intelligent recognition method for building structural materials based on multi‑modal data fusion is proposed. First, a prompting method based on a multi‑modal large language model is designed to generate structured text descriptions tailored to material classification tasks, covering discriminative information such as surface characteristics, geometric details, signs of degradation, and material inference. It introduces a lightweight text feature transformer that reshapes the global vector from the Contrastive Language‑Image Pre‑training (CLIP) text encoder into a sequence and adds positional encoding. The model adopts a decision‑level learnable weighted fusion strategy, where the decision results from the image and text modalities are fused through a learnable linear layer, enabling efficient cross‑modal integration without complex feature alignment. papers.title: Assessment of the Relative Efficiency of Bootstrap Resampling Methods for Forecast Uncertainty Quantification in Nigerian Macroeconomic Time Series: Evidence from Inflation and Exchange Rate Data (1960-2025)
papers.abstract: Quantifying forecast uncertainty is a prerequisite for responsible use of time series models in Nigerian macroeconomic analysis, yet researchers rarely benchmark resampling schemes used to estimate that uncertainty against alternatives on long-run Nigerian data. This study compares three bootstrap procedures for response time series the stationary bootstrap, the moving block bootstrap, and the sieve bootstrap across five ARIMA data-generating processes of increasing complexity: ARIMA(1,0,0), ARIMA(1,1,0), ARIMA(1,1,1), ARIMA(2,1,1), and ARIMA(1,1,3). The simulation design follows a Monte Carlo framework comparable to earlier benchmarking studies. The same three methods are then applied to two real Nigerian macroeconomic series: annual headline inflation (World Bank/FRED, 1960-2025, 66 observations) and the log of the annual NGN/USD exchange rate (Penn World Table/FRED, 1960-2023, 64 observations), both considerably longer than the short annual series used in prior comparative work of this kind. Across all five simulated data-generating processes and both empirical series, the stationary bootstrap yielded the lowest mean squared error (MSE) of one-step-ahead forecasts; the moving block bootstrap was a close second throughout; the sieve bootstrap was markedly less accurate, particularly for integrated I(1) processes. These results diverge from prior work suggesting block-based methods are dominated by ARMA processes with genuine moving-average components, and from work favouring the sieve bootstrap for autoregressive-dominated series. Possible explanations are discussed, including the sensitivity of the sieve reconstruction step to compounding during re-integration of a differenced series. The scope limitations of a reduced-scale Monte Carlo design are noted, and further replication is identified as necessary before firm practical guidance can be issued to Nigerian forecasting practitioners.

Within this context, the present study examines the association between a Game-Based Learning (GBL) strategy and the development of sustainability, ethics, and social responsibility (SER) competencies among engineering students. The study adopted a quantitative, quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test measurements for the experimental group ( n = 84) and a baseline comparison with a reference control group ( n = 22) was assessed only at pre-test, owing to logistical and curricular time constraints at the end of the academic term. The intervention consisted of a GBL experience designed to foster critical reflection, responsible decision-making, and a systemic understanding of the potential social and environmental impacts of engineering practice. The results revealed statistically significant post-test improvements across all assessed competencies within the experimental group, with sustainability exhibiting the largest effect size among the three domains. Although causal inferences should be interpreted with caution due to the study design, the findings suggest that GBL may contribute positively to the development of SER competencies in engineering education. Consequently, the strategic integration of active learning methodologies into engineering curricula may represent a promising approach for promoting more holistic, ethical, and sustainability-oriented professional formation.

papers.title: Staged Multi-Fidelity Optimization of F-Shape Concrete Roadside Barriers: A Surrogate-Assisted Methodology Linking Structural Pre-Screening to Standards-Based Crash Validation
papers.abstract: Roadside barrier design remains constrained by an expensive verification pathway: full-scale crash testing is indispensable for certification, yet it is destructive, costly, and poorly suited to iterative exploration of a large geometric design space. High-fidelity explicit finite element (FE) crash models reduce this burden, but direct optimization using repeated nonlinear vehicle-barrier simulations can still require substantial computational effort. This paper proposes a staged multi-fidelity methodology that deliberately separates early structural screening from final crashworthiness verification. The framework begins with a low-cost equivalent-impact FE model of an F-shape reinforced-concrete barrier, uses a Box-Behnken design and response surface methodology to quantify geometry-response relationships, and embeds the resulting surrogate equations in a Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) search. Candidate designs are then passed through an adaptive boundary check and a fidelity-escalation gate before only a small, shortlisted set is evaluated using explicit nonlinear vehicle-barrier simulations and, ultimately, standards-based physical testing. The approach is motivated by a review of FE-based barrier research from 2015 through 2026, including recent surrogate, Bayesian, neural-network, and evolutionary optimization studies, and directly addresses the need for computationally efficient optimization without treating simplified structural models as substitutes for MASH or EN 1317 certification. Proof-of-concept dissertation data demonstrate the screening stage using 17 Box-Behnken runs for top width, upper-wall offset, and impact-face projection. The preliminary surrogate identifies a boundary candidate of 184 mm, 19 mm, and 203 mm, respectively, with predicted reductions of 5.44% in total deformation and 6.49% in equivalent stress relative to the baseline geometry. These outcomes are interpreted as structural pre-screening results, not as evidence of certified crashworthiness. The principal contribution is therefore methodological: matching model fidelity to the decision being made, reserving expensive nonlinear crash simulations and physical tests for designs that have already survived a transparent, statistically supported screening process.

papers.title: Multi-horizon vessel trajectory prediction with a physically constrained TCN–KAN framework
papers.abstract: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is essential for maritime situational awareness, traffic management, and autonomous navigation. However, existing data-driven methods often struggle to simultaneously represent temporal dependencies at different scales, nonlinear maneuver-induced deviations, and kinematic consistency, particularly as the forecasting horizon increases. This study proposes TCN–KAN–PINN, a unified framework combining a multi-scale causal Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), a parallel Linear-KAN predictor, and physics-informed training. The TCN encoder uses hierarchical dilated residual blocks and sample-specific scale fusion to extract complementary temporal features from historical AIS observations. The Linear Base Pathway models the dominant motion trend, whereas the KAN Residual Pathway learns nonlinear corrections associated with vessel maneuvers. A time-discretized kinematic residual further penalizes discrepancies between predicted coordinate increments and expected displacements derived from vessel motion states, while Relative Loss Balancing with Random Lookback (ReLoBRaLo) adaptively balances the data and physics objectives. The model directly generates a complete 30-step future trajectory, with the 5 min, 15 min, and 30 min results evaluated as prefixes of the same output. Experiments on a real-world AIS dataset show that the proposed framework achieves the best overall trajectory accuracy among representative kinematic and deep learning baselines while maintaining favorable speed and course consistency and practical inference efficiency. Results reported as mean ± standard deviation over five independent runs indicate stable predictive performance. Ablation studies further show that kinematic supervision benefits prediction from the early forecasting steps, whereas the contribution of the KAN pathway becomes more pronounced at medium and long horizons.

papers.abstract: High renewable penetration requires coal-fired units to provide faster and more reliable load-ramping support, while time-varying uncertainties such as coal-quality fluctuation and equipment aging aggravate model-plant mismatch and degrade MPC tracking performance. This paper proposes a kernel-bandwidth adaptive particle filter-model predictive control (KBAPF-MPC) strategy for rapid load-ramping control of thermal power units. The residual prediction error is formulated as an output-equivalent mismatch and estimated online by a particle filter with kernel-bandwidth adaptive diffusion. The diffusion bandwidth is updated from the empirical particle distribution using Silverman’s rule and the effective sample size, providing an adaptive mismatch-estimation mechanism for rapid load-ramping operation. A conditional local practical-stability analysis is provided under bounded mismatch-estimation errors, bounded reference variations, local recursive feasibility, and a practical cost-decrease condition. The analysis characterizes a residual tracking region and establishes a time-average tracking-error bound in terms of the mismatch-estimation-error and reference-variation bounds. The estimated mismatch is embedded into the MPC prediction as a feedforward compensation term while retaining the original optimizer and physical constraints. Simulations on a 350 MW CFB unit with composite parameter drift show that KBAPF-MPC reduces RMSE by 60.7%, 61.9%, and 75.5% compared with conventional MPC, and by 30.7%, 41.5%, and 49.3% compared with UKF-MPC for power output, main steam pressure, and temperature, respectively, while maintaining constraint-compliant actuator responses and real-time feasibility under the considered scenario.

papers.title: Uncertainty-guided active transfer for robotic suction grasping via evidential learning
papers.abstract: Robust uncertainty quantification is crucial for accurate scene understanding and reliable decision-making in robotic suction grasping. Although existing data-driven grasp detection methods demonstrate effectiveness, they often fail to quantify predictive uncertainty and suffer from low sample efficiency during simulation-to-reality transfer. To address these limitations, we propose an uncertainty-guided active transfer framework that leverages evidential deep learning to jointly estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties for evaluating model confidence and environmental ambiguity. Building on this quantification, an asynchronous training pipeline is introduced, driven by a hybrid sampling strategy that iteratively selects both highly uncertain and highly certain target-domain samples. This strategy optimally balances domain exploration with model exploitation, facilitating discriminative training to bridge the simulation-to-reality gap while enhancing sample efficiency. Furthermore, we design an evidential feature fusion mechanism that synergistically integrates the predictive distributions of suction seal quality and the object’s center of mass with their associated uncertainties. By incorporating these uncertainty estimates into the final grasp extraction pipeline, our framework ensures informed decision-making and robust execution. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed uncertainty-driven approach significantly enhances learning efficiency, achieving consistently reliable grasping performance across diverse and complex real-world scenarios.

papers.abstract: Mechanically reliable fused-filament-fabricated (FFF) PLA/OMMT parts depend not only on filler fraction and nominal printing settings, but also on the coupled evolution of clay dispersion, melt rheology, thermal healing, void topology, and strain localization. This study develops C³M-OMMT Twin, a six-stage causal process-structure-property digital twin comprising ExfoRheo-MAP, ThermoBond-Sense, MorphoFrac-3D, CauPSP-Net, ConBayes-Pareto, and CounterTwinV. Approximately 60 D -optimal material-process combinations were used for model development and 20 Bayesian-selected trials were reserved for experimental closure. The design space covered 0–5 wt% OMMT, 195–225 °C nozzle temperature, 0.10–0.25 mm layer height, 25–55 mm s⁻¹ print speed, raster orientation, and infill. A directly characterized condition at 2 wt% OMMT, 215 °C, 0.15 mm, and 35 mm s⁻¹ produced 62.5 MPa tensile strength and approximately 2.2% void fraction. On held-out data, CauPSP-Net achieved R²= 0.974, RMSE= 1.72 MPa, MAE= 1.29 MPa, and MAPE= 2.53%; 90% conformal intervals achieved 90.7% empirical coverage with a 4.46 MPa mean width. Model-based multi-objective optimization identified the same operating neighborhood, with predicted Young's modulus of 3.82 GPa, flexural strength of 94.1 MPa, and CVIFSI of 0.162, while CounterTwinV reported a 3.1% validation discrepancy. The originality lies in retaining physically interpretable intermediate states from exfoliation and rheology through thermal bonding and three-dimensional defect morphology, then separating direct and morphology-mediated effects under calibrated uncertainty. The resulting manufacturing window is intended for reproducible, morphology-aware optimization of lightweight PLA/OMMT FFF components rather than unrestricted extrapolation beyond the validated material and process domain.

papers.title: Towards rapid fatigue assessment of UHPC for wind turbine towers: A sparse-data-driven prediction framework via DeepONet with latent vector adaptation
papers.abstract: Rapid assessment of high-cycle fatigue degradation in ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) is constrained by the long duration of full-lifecycle fatigue testing. This study develops an uncertainty-aware Bayesian transfer learning framework (U-BTL) that combines Deep Operator Networks with specimen-specific latent adaptation to reconstruct long-term stiffness-degradation trajectories from sparse early-cycle observations. During Stage I, operator learning is supported by measured source trajectories, low-weight Weibull-IDW augmentation restricted to the experimentally supported source domain, an exact initial-stiffness boundary K ( 0 ) = 1 , an irreversible-degradation constraint, and a terminal-stiffness surrogate. During Stage II, the pretrained operator is frozen and a specimen-specific latent vector is calibrated probabilistically from a fixed early-cycle observation window. The posterior uncertainty is subsequently propagated to long-term stiffness and threshold-crossing predictions. The evaluation distinguishes interpolation validation from fully held-out out-of-distribution conditions involving an unseen fiber configuration and an unseen stress level. The results demonstrate that Bayesian latent adaptation can reduce specimen-specific prediction bias while providing probabilistic uncertainty bounds for future degradation trajectories. The present validation is restricted to constant-amplitude laboratory UHPC specimens; therefore, the proposed framework is interpreted as a constitutive-level fatigue-prognosis kernel whose future integration into wind-turbine structural monitoring requires additional variable-amplitude, structural-scale, and field validation.

papers.title: A Hybrid Computational Intelligence Framework for Automatic Calibration of Catchment Scale Hydrodynamic Flood Models
papers.abstract: Abstract This study presents a novel automated framework for the calibration and validation of rain-on-grid (RoG) hydrodynamic models at the catchment scale, with specific application to the TUFLOW HPC platform. The proposed approach establishes an integrated and automated workflow that links rainfall input directly to flood response, enabling efficient calibration of key hydraulic parameters, including Manning’s roughness, initial loss, and continuous loss. The framework combines ensemble-based parameter sampling, automated model execution, data-driven surrogate modelling, and evolutionary optimization algorithms (EAs) to systematically explore parameter combinations within the defined calibration ranges. Three modelling techniques—Random Forest (RF), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Gradient Boosting (GB)—are employed to approximate model responses from an ensemble of hydrodynamic model simulations, thereby accelerating the calibration process and reducing computational costs. Furthermore, three EAs, consisting of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO), and Differential Evolution (DE), are applied. The optimization objective is defined as minimizing the discrepancy between simulated and reference inundation extents, quantified through total inundated area derived from benchmark inundation datasets. The entire process is implemented in a MATLAB-based script that automatically controls TUFLOW simulations, iteratively adjusts parameters, and evaluates model performance without manual intervention. The framework is tested in a small catchment case study under multiple design rainfall events (50-, 100-, and 500-year return periods). Results demonstrate close agreement between the simulated and reference inundation areas, with differences of less than 1% across all scenarios. These findings indicate satisfactory predictive performance within the studied calibration range. The key novelty of this study lies in the integration of surrogate-assisted optimization within a fully automated calibration environment tailored for RoG models. Furthermore, the developed MATLAB code is made publicly available via GitHub, promoting transparency, reproducibility, and potential broader application in hydrodynamic flood modelling.

papers.title: Physics-informed hybrid machine learning for predicting effects of metal oxide nano additives on performance and emissions of biodiesel-fueled engines
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the performance and emission characteristics of nanoparticle-enhanced biodiesel-fueled compression ignition engines is essential for efficient engine optimization, cleaner combustion, and reducing experimental costs and time. This study integrates combustion physics with stacked ensemble learning to develop a physics-informed Bayesian-optimized hybrid (PIBoH) framework to simultaneously predict brake thermal efficiency (BTE), brake-specific fuel consumption (BSFC), hydrocarbon (HC), carbon monoxide (CO), and nitrogen oxide (NO x ) emissions. A comprehensive experimental database was compiled from published studies covering diverse biodiesel feedstocks, metal oxide nanoparticles, and engine operating conditions. To embed domain knowledge into the learning process, conventional categorical descriptors were replaced with physically meaningful fuel-property variables, a quantitative additive overall effectiveness index, and seven physics-informed engineered features. Bayesian optimization was employed to fine-tune hyperparameters of the PIBoH framework. The designed framework predicted 298 datasets with average absolute relative deviations of 4.48%, 3.44%, 5.42%, 6.63%, and 5.30% for BTE, BSFC, HC, CO, and NO x , respectively, corresponding to coefficients of determination of 0.9543, 0.9808, 0.9924, 0.9934, and 0.9901. Applicability-domain analysis further demonstrated reliable prediction stability across the investigated operating conditions. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified fuel density and engine load as the dominant variables governing both engine performance and pollutant formation.

papers.title: Spatial Acoustic-Function Partitioning in Gradient Porous Materials for Broadband Sound Absorption
papers.abstract: The growing demand for noise control in transportation, urban environments, and advanced equipment systems is driving sound-absorbing materials toward broader bandwidths, lower weight, and more compact configurations. Conventional porous materials dissipate acoustic energy mainly through thermoviscous friction near pore walls. Under low-frequency and thin-layer conditions, however, their performance is often constrained by the need to reduce incident reflection while maintaining sufficient energy loss within a limited thickness. Existing reviews on porous sound-absorbing materials have mostly been organized around material categories, structural parameters, theoretical models, or fabrication routes, while the common physical basis by which different gradient architectures achieve broadband absorption has rarely been discussed from a unified sound-energy management perspective. Here, we use spatial acoustic-function partitioning as an interpretive framework linking depth-dependent structural variation to the frequency-dependent input impedance, internal acoustic field, and irreversible energy loss. These acoustic functions are not tied to fixed geometric layers and may shift with frequency, boundary conditions, and the gradient profile. The discussion draws on established acoustic models to connect depth-dependent structural variation with impedance, field redistribution, and irreversible loss. Three representative routes are considered: parameter gradients in dual-gradient microperforated networks, multiscale interfacial gradients in gradient fiber/aerogel–porous scaffold composites, and continuous topological gradients in triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures. The roles of additive manufacturing and intelligent design in realizing and optimizing these structures are also discussed. Representative quantitative studies show that no single-gradient profile is universally optimal: Monotonic, reversed, and non-monotonic profiles can each be favorable depending on the complete absorber configuration and target frequency range. Manufacturing fidelity and physics-constrained inverse design are discussed in terms of whether numerically optimized structures can be fabricated reliably and tested experimentally.

papers.abstract: A common challenge educators face is effectively carrying out their duties, particularly given that many students currently struggle to grasp the material or lack enthusiasm for *Aqidah Akhlaq* (Islamic creed and ethics) lessons. This issue may stem from students' passivity during the teaching-learning process or from monotonous teaching styles that breed apathy. Furthermore, teachers must balance instructional methods with the goal of shaping students' Islamic character. Consequently, teachers need to skillfully select appropriate strategies—specifically active learning methods—which offer various ways to engage students both inside and outside the classroom. This study addresses two main questions: how active learning methods are applied to shape Islamic character in the Grade VIII *Aqidah Akhlaq* course at MTs Al-Istiqomah NW Bedus Loteng, and what factors either hinder or support this implementation. The author employs a qualitative research approach, utilizing data collection techniques such as observation, interviews, and documentation. The findings indicate that the implementation of active learning methods in the *Aqidah Akhlaq* course at MTs Al-Istiqomah NW Bedus Loteng has proceeded well, despite some remaining shortcomings. Specific active learning methods utilized include the Jigsaw (expert team model), collaborative learning groups, and Think-Pair-Share. Supporting factors include the teachers, the students, and the availability of adequate facilities and learning resources; conversely, inhibiting factors include a lack of interest among students and teachers, inadequate learning facilities, and an unfavorable environment.

papers.title: Rapid prediction of vehicle body aerodynamics using an active learning-enhanced graph neural network
papers.abstract: Achieving rapid aerodynamic prediction for vehicles under multiple operating conditions is a key challenge in the field of vehicle aerodynamic design. To address this, this study first developed a Graph Neural Network (GNN) surrogate model utilizing a Graph Attention Network (GAT) encoder for force-pressure dual-head prediction. Aerodynamic predictions were performed across the parameter space of various models and operating conditions, and three active learning strategies—uncertainty sampling, diversity sampling and hybrid sampling to the model to improve data efficiency. The results indicate that the GNN-based alternative model performs well in carrying out aerodynamic prediction tasks within the parameter space, with test R 2 values of 0.990 and 0.978 for the force coefficient and pressure distribution, respectively. Active learning strategies significantly improve data utilization efficiency, with the hybrid strategy demonstrating a marked lead in data efficiency ( η 95 = 0 . 22 ), achieving 95% of the performance obtained from training on the full dataset whilst reducing the data volume by 78%. This study successfully applies active learning to the rapid aerodynamic prediction of vehicle-like body models under multiple operating conditions, providing an efficient solution for the rapid iterative development of vehicle aerodynamics.
